intent: Phase 1 of NEXT_SESSION_PROMPT.md's 250-line-cap campaign: bring focus_owner/android/.../EnforcementRunner.kt (564 lines) under the cap.
changes: Extracted four cohesive concerns out of EnforcementRunner into standalone files: LocationAcquisition (fix acquisition -- cached/active/stale fallback), HomeLocationStore (read/write home_location.json), PolicyPinning (VPN/DNS pin + visibility sweep applied during apply()), SweepablePackages (the installed-package enumeration used by decide())

EnforcementRunner's public API is unchanged -- acquireLocation, setHomeToCurrentLocation, hasHomeLocation all still exist as delegating wrappers, since MainActivity.kt calls setHomeToCurrentLocation/hasHomeLocation directly on an EnforcementRunner instance

EnforcementRunner.best(...) -- a companion object function called directly by the existing EnforcementRunnerBestTest.kt -- was deliberately NOT moved; it stays on EnforcementRunner and LocationAcquisition's internal cachedFix() calls back into it, avoiding any test-file change
EnforcementRunner.ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_MS and FRESH_WINDOW_MS constants kept as aliases pointing at LocationAcquisition's copies, to preserve the public constant names without duplicating the values
EnforcementRunner.kt: 564 -> 237 lines; four new files at 198/116/94/42 lines
No behavioral change: every moved method/function body is verbatim

verification.evidence: EnforcementRunner.kt off the list; file count over cap dropped from 9 to 8

BUILD SUCCESSFUL; test-results XML shows 40 tests total (6+9+12+13), 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped. EnforcementRunnerBestTest (6 tests) specifically confirms EnforcementRunner.best(...) still resolves and behaves identically after the split, since that test calls it by name and was not modified

risks: No dedicated unit test exists for EnforcementRunner.decide()/apply() themselves (they depend on Android system services -- LocationManager, PackageManager, DevicePolicyManager -- not unit-testable without instrumentation), so the decide/apply orchestration split relies on compile-time type-checking plus the unchanged public API surface, same limitation as the DevicePolicyBridge split this session

PolicyPinning.kt bundles two only loosely related concerns (policy pinning + visibility sweep) in one file rather than two, to keep the file count and per-file complexity down given how much was already extracted from EnforcementRunner this session -- a future split could separate them further if PolicyPinning.kt itself grows
rollback: After rollback, re-run gradlew compileDebugKotlin test --rerun-tasks to confirm the pre-split file still compiles and the same 40 tests pass
